results.content: AdamW(learning_rate =0.001, weight_decay =0.004, beta_1 =0.9, beta_2 =0.999, epsilon =1e-07, amsgrad = False, clipnorm = None, clipvalue = None, global_clipnorm = None, use_ema = False, ema_momentum =0.99, ema_overwrite_frequency = None, loss_scale_factor = None, gradient_accumulation_steps = None, name = "adamw",** kwargs). AdamW optimization is a stochastic gradient descent method that is based on adaptive estimation of first-order and second-order moments with an added method to decay weights per the techniques discussed in the paper, 'Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization' by Loshchilov, Hutter et al., 2019. EMA consists of computing an exponential moving average of the weights of the model (as the weight values change after each training batch), and periodically overwriting the weights with their moving average. If an int, model & optimizer variables will not be updated at every step; instead they will be updated every `gradient_accumulation_steps` steps, using the average value of the gradients since the last update. EMA frequency will look at "accumulated" iterations value (optimizer steps // gradient\_accumulation\_steps).

results.content: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks Zhao Chen 1 Vijay Badrinarayanan 1 Chen-Yu Lee 1 Andrew Rabinovich 1 Abstract Deep multitask networks, in which one neural net-work produces multiple predictive outputs, can offer better speed and performance than their single-task counterparts but are challenging to train properly. We show that for various network architectures, for both regres-sion and classiﬁcation tasks, and on both synthetic and real datasets, GradNorm improves accuracy and reduces overﬁtting across multiple tasks when compared to single-task networks, static baselines, and other adaptive multitask loss balancing tech-niques. The correct balance is struck when tasks are train-ing at similar rates; if task i is training relatively quickly, then its weight wi(t) should decrease relative to other task weights wj(t)|j̸=i to allow other tasks more inﬂuence on GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks training.
